sources.entry: go2rtc | Camera streaming application supporting RTSP, WebRTC and HomeKit

summary.one_liner: go2rtc is a zero-dependency camera streaming application that ingests and re-serves video/audio streams over RTSP, WebRTC, HomeKit, HLS, MJPEG and other protocols.
summary.what_it_does: It reads streams from many camera and device protocols (RTSP, RTMP, ONVIF, WebRTC, HomeKit, plus vendor-specific ones like Tapo, Tuya, Wyze, Ring and Dahua-style NVRs) and re-publishes them as RTSP, WebRTC, MSE/MP4, HLS, MJPEG, FLV, MPEG-TS and HomeKit outputs. It auto-matches codecs to what the client supports and uses FFmpeg only when transcoding is needed. It supports two-way audio to cameras that have speakers, can mix audio tracks from several sources, and can publish streams to services such as YouTube and Telegram via RTMP/RTMPS. A WebUI and HTTP/WebSocket API show active connection stats and let you edit the go2rtc.yaml config. Releases are provided as binaries for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, plus Docker images and a Home Assistant add-on.
use_cases: restream RTSP camera feeds to a browser with low latency
view home security cameras through WebRTC or MSE
add two-way audio or play sound files through supported cameras
feed camera streams to Home Assistant or Frigate for recording
publish a camera stream to YouTube or Telegram
expose a HomeKit or MJPEG view of a camera that lacks native support
how_to_run: Download the binary for your OS from the latest release (or use the Docker image alexxit/go2rtc)
On Linux or macOS run: chmod +x go2rtc_xxx_xxx
Create a go2rtc.yaml with a streams section, e.g. hall-camera: rtsp://user:password@192.168.1.123/...
Run go2rtc from the directory containing go2rtc.yaml
Open the web interface on port 1984
Optionally restrict api, rtsp and webrtc listen addresses in the config for security
notable: Zero-dependency single binary for Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD and many ARM/MIPS devices
Multi-source two-way codec negotiation across several inputs for one stream
Built-in PCMA/PCMU/PCM repackaging to FLAC for MSE/MP4/HLS and resampling for WebRTC
Codec filters in stream URLs (e.g. ?video=h264&audio=aac) to select tracks
Can be imported as a library into other Go projects
caveats: The HTTP API can reach insecure sources such as exec and echo; the README warns that an exposed API gives full server access and recommends restricting modules and paths
Web interface has no built-in auth outside the Home Assistant add-on; a reverse proxy is needed for protection
Some vendor integrations (e.g. Nest) rely on user-unfriendly or paid APIs, and Wyze legacy access uses docker-wyze-bridge
Master branch builds may be unstable
